title: Trade-off between predictability and quantum coherence for multi-path interferometry and its operational interpretation
abstract: The complementarity principle is a cornerstone of quantum mechanics. In this work, we investigate a complementarity relation between the predictability and quantum coherence, respectively, representing the particle-like and wave-like behaviour in wave--particle duality, in a multi-path setup. We introduce a basis-dependent predictability defined by the Bures distance between the state dephased in the chosen basis and the maximally mixed state. The predictability depends only on the observed basis statistics and admits a closed form in terms of the Bhattacharyya overlap. We derive a trade-off relation between the predictability and a coherence measure defined based on the nonclassicality of the Kirkwood--Dirac quasiprobability. For pure states, the trade-off relation is an exact equality. Remarkably, this wave--particle duality relation endows the coherence measure with an operational interpretation as the classically irreducible part of measurement randomness, yielding a tight worst-case bound on the guessing probability in source-independent QRNG.
summary: This paper establishes a quantitative complementarity relation between predictability and quantum coherence in multi-path interferometry. It defines these quantities using advanced metrics like the Bures distance and proves that this duality has an operational meaning: coherence quantifies the portion of measurement uncertainty irreducible by any classical side information. This provides a tight bound relevant for quantum random number generation.
main_problem: The work investigates a complementarity relation between predictability (particle-like behavior) and quantum coherence (wave-like behavior) in multi-path interferometry.
main_result: A trade-off relation, $eC + eP \le 1$, is established for mixed states, which endows the coherence measure with an operational interpretation as the classically irreducible part of measurement randomness.
method: The analysis defines predictability using the Bures distance on dephased states and derives a complementary bound involving this metric and a convex-roof construction applied to coherence measures.
model_or_system: The theoretical framework is built around multi-path interferometry setups, analyzing quantum states ($ho$) undergoing measurement in a specified basis $\{\Pi_a\}$.
key_observables: Predictability ($P$), Quantum Coherence ($C$), Bures distance ($D_B$), and the classical-label conditional min-entropy.
important_parameters: The dimensionality of the system ($d$) and the specific measurement basis $\{\Pi_a\}$ are key parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on defining coherence as a monotone satisfying properties like convexity, faithfulness, and monotonicity under decoherence.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate plots showing normalized coherence ($\epsilon_C$) versus polar angle for qubits, and geometric interpretations relating coherence to the Bures distance between dephased states.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining predictability via Bures distance in multi-path setups, deriving a complementarity relation for pure states as an equality, extending this to mixed states using convex roofs, proving mathematical properties of the coherence measure, and finally establishing operational bounds related to quantum randomness.
why_interesting: This work provides a fundamental resource theory perspective on wave-particle duality, linking geometric measures (Bures distance) directly to information-theoretic concepts like classical randomness and quantum source security.
